newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 11.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 11.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday morning:
** Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda tells business leaders the government will review minimum tax on companies at the time of the annual budget in February
** The Securities and Exchange Board of India allows new stock exchanges, permits rights issues by mutual funds
** The Indian cabinet will consider state-run Videsh Sanchar Nigam plan to raise $500 million through global depositary receipts issue, the Financial Express reports
It will also consider a seven percent divestment
** The Finance Ministry plans to allow new infrastructure firms, especially in road and port privatisation projects, to tap world markets before going public domestically, the Economic Times reports
** The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) declares two brokers as defaulters for not honouring commitments; takes cue from the National Stock Exchange which declared three members as defaulters on Monday
The defaults followed huge losses after prices slumped
** The Indian rupee INR= opened steady at 35.87/88 per dollar and seen range-bound, dealers say
** Indian shares ended in negative territory on Tuesday but off their lows on news the government will look afresh into a controversial tax, brokers said
** The BSE top-30 index .BSESN ended 16.49 points lower at 2,798.57 after dipping to 2,782.03.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange .NSEI index was down 5.49 points at 803.20, off 797.66 day's low.
